items.title: Window chrome polish
items.detail: The Feedback form no longer pops a redundant "Feedback" tooltip on hover. The fullscreen button always sits on the editor-facing side of a window's bar (right side in the left panel, left side in the right panel, beside the pop-out). And the header icons are one height now — the × grew and the fullscreen arrows shrank to match the pop-out chevron.

items.title: Note colors: the current color never moves
items.detail: Opening the color row on a note or to-do keeps the current color exactly where the dot was — the custom + swatch sits at the far end instead of displacing it.

items.title: Every side-panel window can go fullscreen
items.detail: One fullscreen button in every window's top row (and dock accordion) takes that tool over the editor area — same chrome rows, same body, with Return to Editor in the ribbon and a × in the header. One takeover at a time by construction. Excluded: the Scrapbook (its surface is already a takeover) and the fixed-size Title Page.

items.title: Scenes: List and Cards offer the same four controls
items.detail: Filter, Reorder, View, and Search now all work in both views. The card wall obeys the filter and search (count shows the fraction); the list gains the same drag-reorder mode as the cards — grips, was→now badges, and the Undo/Redo/Cancel/Apply bar. While reordering, every scene shows regardless of filters (applying rewrites the whole script order).

items.title: Any color for notes
items.detail: The note color dots gain a custom swatch — the same wide-open color picker the Characters window uses. Works on general note cards and on script-note popovers (the highlight recolors to match); card backgrounds get a soft pastel of whatever you pick. The six classic colors are unchanged.

items.title: One tab style: the Goals look
items.detail: The file-tab style is retired. All side-panel window tabs — Characters, Production Tags, Analytics, and the shared window chrome — are now the segmented control from Goals, with the active tab filled blue. The Characters window background returns to the single side-panel color it had before the file-tab experiment.

items.title: View menu: one Zoom, seated with the window controls
items.detail: The native window-menu item macOS labels "Zoom" (maximize) is gone — it read as a duplicate of the page-zoom submenu. Zoom, Minimize, and Toggle Full Screen now sit together as View's final section.

items.title: Navigator scene numbers moved to the right
items.detail: With the toggle on, the number sits at the right edge of each scene row instead of before the heading.

items.title: Focus window: cleaner enable flow
items.detail: "Enable Focus Tool" (capital T), the explainer text lives behind a ? button now, and everything below the master switch dims and locks while the tool is off.

items.title: Workspaces window carries the full menu
items.detail: Save Changes to this Workspace, Reset to Saved Layout, Edit Workspaces…, and Import Workspaces from a Project… now sit below the workspace list — the same actions the View → Workspaces menu offers, one implementation behind both.

items.title: Feedback form loads instantly
items.detail: The form loads once at app start and stays alive in the background, so opening the Feedback window shows it immediately instead of a blank frame.

items.title: Scenes fullscreen shows the View options
items.detail: The fullscreen takeover now carries the same control cluster as the Scenes window — Filter, Reorder, View, and Search — over the same body, so you can switch between List and Cards (and filter or search the list) without leaving fullscreen. The fullscreen button is available from both views now, not just Cards.

items.title: Notes and To-Do are for non-script items only
items.detail: Script-anchored notes and script [ ] to-do lists no longer appear in the Notes and To-Do windows — those live in the Navigator, which lists them and jumps to them (to-dos tick right in the Navigator, and in the script itself). The windows hold only general cards now, so their In-Script/General filter and Scene # sort are gone; Sort keeps Manual and Date Created.

items.title: Script notes edit in a popover on the highlight
items.detail: A note anchored in the script opens right where it lives: click its highlight (or right-click → Edit Note, or the toolbar/Insert Note actions) and a sticky-card popover appears on the spot — title, text with @asset references and media previews, color dots that recolor the highlight, and delete. Clicking a note in the Navigator jumps to the highlight and opens the same popover.

items.title: Scenes fullscreen no longer traps you
items.detail: Fullscreen from the Scenes cards view is now an editor-area takeover like Characters: the toolbar, side rails, and status bar stay put, a Return to Editor button sits in the ribbon, and the takeover header carries its own ×. The old fullscreen covered the entire app with no way out.

items.title: Scenes window wears the standard chrome
items.detail: The in-body count row is gone: the scene count sits beside the window title, the fullscreen button moved to the top row, and Reorder moved up beside the View control (cards view). While reordering, an Undo/Redo/Cancel/Apply bar appears above the cards.

items.title: Navigator: scene numbers, standard Filter, and search
items.detail: A # toggle on the left of the second row shows or hides scene numbers before each scene name. The old funnel popover is now the standard text Filter dropdown (per-kind show/hide), and the row gains the standard search to narrow by keyword.

items.title: Design window remembers what you collapsed
items.detail: All Design sections start minimized, and the open/closed state you leave behind survives closing the window (and the app).

items.title: Relationship map opens at the right size
items.detail: The map no longer flashes oversized icons before shrinking to fit — it computes its frame before first paint, including when saved node positions exist.

items.title: The larger carets, everywhere
items.detail: Revised icon-audit pick: every caret and disclosure chevron now uses the larger (Fa) chevron family — dropdown triggers, dock accordions, tree and group disclosure arrows, Structure/Locations/Tags category rows included.

items.title: More windows on the standard format
items.detail: Locations, Structure, Pages, Production Tags, Notes, To-Do, Snippets, and Highlights now follow the window template: the count sits beside the window title (Structure counts acts), in-body title rows are gone, Tags' eye toggle and View/Manage tabs moved into the window chrome, and Highlights' add button joined the bottom row like Notes and To-Do.

items.title: Scrapbook delete buttons match the theme
items.detail: The page and section delete buttons in the Scrapbook side panel were black regardless of theme; they now use the theme text color like every neighboring control.

items.title: One icon per action, everywhere
items.detail: Every function that wore two or more different icons now wears one, per the icon audit picks: one fullscreen face (the diagonal arrows), × to close, one magnifier for search, plain + to add, an outline trash can for anything that deletes, one chevron family for carets and submenus, one pencil for Rename, the wrench for Settings/Customize, one checkmark, one copy icon, outline eyes for show/hide, matching undo/redo arrows, one reset arrow, the circled ± for zoom, one drag-handle pattern, the outline help circle, ← for back, and one Divider/Spacer pair in Customize.

items.title: No more emoji in the chrome
items.detail: The Navigator's note rows, the Asset Manager's file-type and upload/download markers, and the note-card placeholders now use monotone icons and plain text instead of emoji.

items.title: Smooth image slideshow
items.detail: Stepping through a character's images no longer flashes — the current picture stays up until the next one is ready.

items.title: Quieter footer
items.detail: The status bar no longer announces “Local System - Saved” (a save failure still shows). The current element, runtime and page readouts appear only while the editor itself is on screen — not under the Scrapbook or Characters fullscreen.

items.title: Keyboard Shortcuts moved to Settings
items.detail: Editing hotkeys now lives in Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts (it left Customize). The Help window's shortcut list links straight to it.

items.title: No redundant tooltips
items.detail: Controls that already spell out their name (like the side-panel tool rows) no longer pop a tooltip repeating it. Icon-only buttons keep theirs.

items.title: One takeover at a time
items.detail: Opening the Scrapbook now closes Characters fullscreen and vice versa — the ribbon can no longer end up with two “Return to Editor” buttons. The Characters fullscreen title bar is also tighter above the tabs.

items.title: Window rows never wrap
items.detail: When a tool window gets too narrow for its tabs and controls, the tabs collapse into a single dropdown first; if space is still short, the row scrolls sideways instead of stacking onto extra lines.

items.title: From Script updates itself
items.detail: The Characters > From Script list now follows the script — it refreshes about a second after you stop typing. The Re-scan button is gone.

items.title: Character card fixes
items.detail: The Design window's field-row spacing knob now also moves the gap above Description; the empty image slot reads “+ Add Image”; an opened-but-empty search folds back to its magnifier when you click away.

items.title: Window menu folded into View
items.detail: Minimize, Zoom and Fullscreen now sit at the end of the View menu; the separate Window menu is gone.

items.title: One layout for every tool window
items.detail: Every tool window now follows the same template: a title bar with the tool name and item count centered (pop-in on the left; fullscreen, pop-out and close on the right), and a second row with tabs on the left and quiet Filter / Sort / View / Search controls on the right. The same layout compresses into the side panels — the panel row carries the count and fullscreen button, and the row below it holds the tabs and controls.

items.title: Airtable-style window controls
items.detail: Filter shows a count chip and opens its options in a dropdown; Sort and View open dropdowns (View shows the current view's icon and name); Search is a magnifier that expands into an inline field and collapses with Escape. Characters uses Sort / View / Search (View switches Cards/List in Profiles and List/Map in Relationships); Scenes uses Filter / View / Search — its footer search bar is gone.

items.title: Characters: view choice works everywhere
items.detail: Cards/List now applies in the side panel and floating window too, not just fullscreen, and the choice is remembered. Cards shows the essentials card; List shows compact bars that expand to full info.

items.title: Mores & Continueds moved to Customize
items.detail: The dialogue continuation markers now live in Customize > Editor, next to the element and transition lists. They left Settings.

items.title: Menus always in the macOS menu bar
items.detail: The menus now always live in the real macOS menu bar. The in-window menu option and the Customize > Menu Bar tab are gone.

items.title: Faster hover tooltips
items.detail: Button names now appear after a short pause instead of the long OS delay — the app draws its own tooltip from the same labels, so every control shows its name quickly.

items.title: Customizable transitions
items.detail: Customize ▸ Editor now has a Transitions list: click “Add Transition” to enter your own (they appear as you type in a Transition element), drag to reorder, and hide built-ins you never use. “WIPE TO:” is now a built-in. Built-ins can be hidden but not deleted; your own can be removed.

items.title: New “Editor” tab in Customize
items.detail: The Customize “Elements” tab is now “Editor” and sits at the top of the list (it covers elements and transitions). Customize now opens on this tab by default, the window opens lower so it no longer overlaps the ribbon, and Side Panels moved above Quick Access.

items.title: Per-section “+” on the ribbon editor
items.detail: While customizing the toolbar, every section has its own small + to drop an item, divider, spacer or new section exactly there — instead of two boundary buttons that guessed the section (which is why dividers kept landing in the wrong one).

items.title: Ribbon editor sizing + divider visibility
items.detail: Sections in the toolbar editor no longer render larger than they do on the saved bar — they start compact and grow only as items are added (the section title field no longer forces them wide). Inline dividers now use the same color and weight as full-height section dividers, so they’re no longer hard to see.

items.title: Typewriter tool renamed “Focus”
items.detail: The Typewriter tool is now called “Focus”.

items.title: Backup & Restore settings
items.detail: Settings ▸ General ▸ Backup & Restore exports all your settings and customizations (design, toolbar/ribbon layout, themes, elements, transitions, shortcuts, menu system…) to a file, and imports them into another install — so a release build can inherit everything from the dev app. Sign-in and device tokens are left out for safety. Scripts aren't affected.

items.title: Native menus by default on macOS
items.detail: A fresh install (including a release build, whose storage is separate from the dev app) now defaults to the native macOS menu bar instead of the in-window one. An explicit choice in Settings still wins.

items.title: Updated app logo
items.detail: Swapped in the refined “SC” mark (smaller letters) everywhere the old one lived — the macOS/Windows/iOS/Android app icons, the browser favicon, the loading splash and the About window. The first-run welcome screen also showed the old “OD” monogram; it now shows “SC”.

items.title: Focus centers the last line of the script
items.detail: At the end of the script there was no room to scroll past the last page, so the current line drifted low. The editor area now gets real over-scroll room below the last page (a half-page beyond), so the line stays centered right to the final line — no waiting for a new page.

items.title: Focus tool: one list
items.detail: The Focus tool no longer splits its options under “Scrolling” and “Focus” headings — everything sits together in one list.

items.title: Focus highlight bar fits the page in Extreme focus
items.detail: With “Highlight the current line” and “Extreme focus” both on, the highlight bar was stuck to the left after the layout resized. It now follows the page whenever the window, panels or fullscreen change.

items.title: Character “Full Name” field
items.detail: Characters now have a Full Name field. When you connect a “Referred in Script” name to an existing character (e.g. SAM VEDU → SAM), that full name is filled in automatically.

items.title: New Relationships tab
items.detail: A “Relationships” tab (between Profiles and Relationship Map) lists every relationship in an editable form — change the characters, type, dynamic and description inline, add new relationships, and delete them.

items.title: Character List view fixes
items.detail: The list view now uses the app theme instead of a light-gray “page” (which also leaked onto the Relationship Map tab). List items are wider and more compact so more fit on screen, and each has a left caret showing it toggles open. The Relationship Map close X now matches the other windows (it was too thick).

items.title: Customize ribbon scrolls instead of overlapping
items.detail: When the ribbon was too crowded to fit in Customize mode, sections were squeezed into each other until they overlapped. Now sections keep their spacing and the bar scrolls horizontally so you can reach what runs off-screen.

items.title: Classify names in “Referred in Script”
items.detail: Each name in the Referred-in-Script list now has a Classify menu: mark it as a location, mark it as other, or connect it to an existing character (e.g. “SAM VEDU” → SAM). Any of these files the name away so it drops off the list. Classifications are saved with the script.

items.title: Reworked the character fullscreen header
items.detail: The Profiles / Relationship Map tabs now sit on the same row as the “Characters” title (left-aligned, spaced from it). The right side of that row carries the active tab’s controls — Cards/List for Profiles, or Add Relationship / Fit / the scroll hint for the Relationship Map — and the close X is on the far right.

items.title: Sort moved onto the search row
items.detail: The character Sort dropdown shares the row with the Search field instead of sitting on its own bar.

items.title: List view cards start collapsed
items.detail: In the fullscreen List view each character starts as a compact bar (name + line/scene counts); click it to expand the full profile.

items.title: Relationship dropdowns list every character
items.detail: The Add/Edit Relationship “Character A/B” dropdowns only listed characters scanned from script cues — a character that existed only as a profile or in an existing relationship was missing. They now list every known character.

items.title: Character fullscreen List view follows the theme
items.detail: The fullscreen List view rendered characters as white “pages” with dark text, clashing with the dark theme. It now uses the theme colors like the rest of the app.

items.title: Character tool fullscreen works like the Scrapbook
items.detail: Fullscreen was a fixed overlay that covered the whole window — the status bar painted over its exit button, so there was no way out (you had to hard-quit). Now it fills the editor area like the Scrapbook, leaving the toolbar and status bar intact, with a “Return to Editor” button in the ribbon.

items.title: Relationship map scroll-to-zoom speed is adjustable
items.detail: Scroll-to-zoom in the relationship map was way too fast (and worse on a trackpad). It’s calmer now, and there’s a “Relationship map scroll speed” slider in the Design panel’s new Behavior section to tune it.

items.title: Removed the redundant Connections tab
items.detail: The character tool’s Connections tab is gone; Profiles and Relationship Map remain.

items.title: Editor View button is vertically centered
items.detail: The Editor View big button pinned its “Editor View” label to the bottom of its section instead of centering the dropdown-and-label together like the other big buttons. Now it’s centered like the rest.

items.title: Ribbon top & bottom padding in the Design panel
items.detail: Added “Ribbon top padding” and “Ribbon bottom padding” sliders to the Toolbar / Ribbon section of the Design panel.

items.title: Ribbon shifts up when no section has a title
items.detail: The title band was always reserved (so titled and untitled sections line up). When NO section has a title, that blank strip is now removed and the whole ribbon shifts up — about 15px shorter. If any section is titled, the band stays reserved so the rows still align.

items.title: New app logo
items.detail: Updated the app icon, dock icon, favicon, splash and About-window logo to the new “SC” mark.

items.title: Two-row vertical gap now actually closes the gap
items.detail: The row boxes already touch, so the space you see between the two rows is each row’s height around a smaller icon — a 0 gap couldn’t remove it. The slider now goes negative to pull the two rows of icons together (and positive to spread them), so you can close that gap completely.

items.title: Design panel — finer ribbon spacing and more font knobs
items.detail: The toolbar spacing slider is now three: “Section spacing” (between sections), “Button spacing (in section)” for the small buttons inside a section, and “Two-row vertical gap” for the space between the two rows of a two-row section. Added font-size sliders for more places text lives — navigator panel title & scene synopsis, tool-window title, script-note title, sticky-note snippet (code), scrapbook sidebar heading, dialog field labels — plus dialog input height, index-card badge size, and beat-column header padding. Every new knob was verified to change its target in the running app.

items.title: Design panel — every slider now actually does something
items.detail: The menu/toolbar height, button size and panel width knobs were dead for anyone using a customized bar: those dimensions are owned by the compact/comfortable/custom modes and the drag handles (and set inline), so a styling variable could never win. Those knobs are gone; menu and toolbar “Item spacing” now drive that same system so they work in every mode, and the surviving sliders (radii, icon/label sizes, card/dialog/scrapbook/beatboard/navigator details) were each verified against the running app. A note explains that a setting only shows while the thing it styles is on screen. Chrome sizes still live on the bars’ own resize handles and the size modes; page geometry stays in Page Setup.

items.title: Design panel — fixed the dead sliders
items.detail: Some knobs wrote into the void: the ribbon “Small button width” was shadowed by a more specific rule, the separator-margin knob did nothing in the ribbon, and the page width/margins/font knobs fought Page Setup (which owns page geometry) so they never moved anything. The width knob now works, the no-op ones are gone, and the whole panel was re-verified against the running app so every remaining slider changes what it says. Page geometry lives in Page Setup, where it belongs.

items.title: Design panel — live design settings
items.detail: View ▸ Design… opens a floating, draggable panel with a slider for every wired design knob (page margins & font, menu bar, toolbar, panels & windows, note cards, Scrapbook, dialogs, beatboard & index cards, navigator & outline). Drag a slider and the app restyles in real time; changes persist. Each knob has a number box and a reset, plus Reset all and a Copy CSS export so a chosen look can be baked in permanently. This replaces sending a note for every small formatting change.

items.title: Small ribbon buttons pulled noticeably tighter
items.detail: v4.6's trim was too subtle to see. The small (two-row) icon boxes are narrower again (compact 26→20px, comfortable 28→22px), the row gap is pinned to 1px, and the wrapper's internal padding is gone — so the icons now read as a tight group. Big buttons are unchanged.

items.title: Ribbon button rows line up across sections
items.detail: A section with a title used to push its buttons lower than a title-less section beside it. Every two-row section now reserves the same title band — empty or not — so all the button rows sit on the same line.

items.title: Lock All also freezes ribbon layout edits
items.detail: While locked you could still add sections and drag items on the ribbon; now the toolbar can't be edited until you unlock (the Customize dialog already tells you to).

items.title: Ribbon height drag-bar is grabbable again
items.detail: The bar on the ribbon's bottom edge for dragging its height is a real 6px strip once more — visible and grabbable when unlocked, invisible when locked, and it never shifts the layout on toggle.

items.title: Logo in the About window
items.detail: The About dialog now shows the app icon at the top.

items.title: Updated app icon, sized for the dock
items.detail: Refreshed the SC icon and gave it the standard transparent margin so it sits at the same size as other macOS dock icons (it was full-bleed and looked oversized).

items.title: Screenshots work again
items.detail: Capturing the whole window had stopped working; it now captures reliably (and crops to the selected area afterwards).

items.title: Ribbon titles no longer cut off
items.detail: Section titles at the top of the ribbon had their tops clipped; the ribbon now leaves room for them.

items.title: Ribbon size drag-bar is back
items.detail: The bar under the ribbon for dragging its height was invisible; it shows again (and still never shifts the layout when you lock/unlock).

items.title: New ScriptCraft app icon
items.detail: The purple "SC" mark is now the app icon (macOS dock + .icns, Windows .ico, the favicon and the loading splash) — replacing the old OpenDraft art.

items.title: Lock button matches the other big buttons
items.detail: The sizing-lock big button now wraps its icon and caption in one button (its hover box covered only the icon before, with the label hanging below), so it lines up with every other big ribbon button.

items.title: Big ribbon icons sized to match
items.detail: Font Awesome glyphs fill their box by different amounts, so framed icons (camera, image, chart…) read smaller than full-bleed ones. Measured every ribbon icon's glyph and scaled the padded ones up so the big buttons look the same height.

items.title: Tighter ribbon spacing, roomier titles
items.detail: Reduced the gaps between buttons and sections, and added more space above the section titles at the top of the ribbon.

items.title: Screenshot icon sized to match
items.detail: The camera icon read smaller than its neighbours (the glyph has more padding); bumped it so the big ribbon icons look the same height.

items.title: Screenshot options drop from the button
items.detail: The Full Screen / Select Area choice now appears as a small dropdown under the Screenshot toolbar button instead of a centered window.

items.title: Screenshot: full screen or a selected area
items.detail: Clicking Screenshot now asks whether to capture the whole screen or to drag out an area to capture.

items.title: Choose where screenshots save
items.detail: Settings ▸ Save Options ▸ Screenshots lets you pick a folder for screenshot PNGs (desktop app); leave it on Downloads for the default.

items.title: Screenshot captures the screen, not the whole script
items.detail: The Screenshot button now grabs the current window as you see it — toolbar, panels, menus and all — cropped to the visible area, instead of rendering the entire multi-page script into one tall image.

items.title: Delete key removes Scrapbook items reliably
items.detail: Selecting an image or table and pressing Delete now removes it even if a text box elsewhere still held the caret (that stale focus was wrongly blocking deletion). Grabbing a box's move bar selects it so Delete removes the whole box; typing in text or a cell still edits.

items.title: Page Zoom +/- icons
items.detail: The +/- icons are 12px and sit right next to the % number.

items.title: Page Zoom +/- sizing
items.detail: Split the difference on the +/- stepper size and tucked them in closer to the % readout.

items.title: No stray transitions list on launch
items.detail: The autofill suggestions (transitions/characters/scene headings) no longer pop up in the top-left corner when the app opens — they only appear while you're actually typing in the editor.

items.title: Delete a selected Scrapbook item
items.detail: Select an image, table or text box (click it, or its move bar) and press Delete or Backspace to remove it. Typing in text or a table cell still edits normally.

items.title: Screenshot button fixed
items.detail: The Screenshot button did nothing because the download never started (WebKit needs the link in the page) and errors were swallowed. It now saves the PNG, works on the Scrapbook too, and reports if it can't.

items.title: Page Zoom +/- actually shrink now
items.detail: The ribbon's big-button styling was overriding the smaller steppers; scoped the zoom sizing so the +/- are small and the % is large as intended.

items.title: Return to Editor on one line
items.detail: The button label is a single row again, centered.

items.title: Page Zoom works on the Scrapbook
items.detail: The toolbar's zoom now scales the Scrapbook board too — boxes, tables and images zoom in and out, and dragging/resizing stays accurate at any zoom.

items.title: Zoom control refined
items.detail: Renamed to "Page Zoom", with smaller +/- steppers and a larger, more legible % readout.

items.title: Return to Editor text centered
items.detail: The two-line Return to Editor button label is centered.

items.title: Scrapbook font picker shows the chosen font
items.detail: While a Scrapbook box is open the Font picker showed Courier Prime no matter what you picked (it was reading the script editor). It now shows the font you applied.

items.title: Scrapbook ribbon: two-line Return button, no title
items.detail: Removed the "Scrapbook" ribbon title; the Return to Editor button is back to two lines ("Return" / "to Editor").

items.title: Scrapbook text formatting works
items.detail: Bold, italic, underline, font, font size and text colour now apply to the selected text in a Scrapbook text box and are saved — before, font/size/colour hit the (empty) script editor and B/I/U changes weren't persisted.

items.title: Right-click a table for its menu
items.detail: Right-clicking a Scrapbook table opens the Table menu (insert/delete rows & columns, background & grid colour, sort…) right at the cursor, acting on the cell you clicked.

items.title: Table background & grid controls
items.detail: "Shading" is now "Background Color", and you can set the grid (border) colour and thickness from the Table menu.

items.title: Clicking into a cell highlights the table
items.detail: The bright table border now appears when you click into a cell, not only when you click the box or its bar.

items.title: Return to Editor on one line
items.detail: The Scrapbook ribbon's Return to Editor button reads on a single row.

items.title: Lock/Unlock no longer nudges the layout
items.detail: The resize strip under the ribbon only existed while unlocked, adding a 5px gap that shifted everything below when you toggled the sizing lock. It no longer takes any layout space.

items.title: Table inserts/deletes fixed for the cell you're in
items.detail: The v3.84 fix missed the case that mattered: the menu bar never removes focus from the cell you clicked, so Insert Row Above copied the active cell upward and Delete Row/Column left the deleted value behind. Table cells now redraw correctly even while focused, so every row/column op acts cleanly on the active cell.

items.title: Table row/column inserts and deletes now land correctly
items.detail: A Scrapbook table cell showed its text only when first drawn, so inserting or deleting a row/column shifted the data but left the cells showing their neighbour's old text — every Table menu op looked like it hit the wrong cell. Cells now stay in sync with the data (the caret is still never disturbed while you type). Insert Row Above/Below and Insert Column Left/Right act relative to the active cell as intended.

items.title: New Return to Editor icon
items.detail: The Scrapbook's Return to Editor button uses the undo-style return arrow.

items.title: Scrapbook stays in the side panel
items.detail: The Scrapbook is panel-bound again — its pop-out button is gone (its writing surface takes over the editor area, so a floating window never made sense).

items.title: Scrapbook ribbon: just Return to Editor
items.detail: The ribbon's Scrapbook section now shows only the Return to Editor button under a standard, centred section title. Insert Picture and Insert Table live in the menu bar's Picture / Table menus.

items.title: Image bar sits above the picture
items.detail: The move/delete bar for a Scrapbook image now floats above the picture instead of overlapping its top edge — same as text boxes and tables.

items.title: Scrapbook text box: accent border when clicked in
items.detail: Reverted the clicked-in text box to its accent border (distinct from hover), matching the focused table box.

items.title: Table grid stays visible while typing
items.detail: A Scrapbook table kept its grid only while empty; typing dropped it to a near-invisible line. The grid now uses one always-on colour, empty or filled.

items.title: Scrapbook can pop out of the side panel
items.detail: The Scrapbook now has the pop-out button like every other tool — it is no longer locked inside the panel.

items.title: Scrapbook table bar hides when you click away
items.detail: A table's move/delete bar now hides once you click off it and returns on hover or when the table is active (images already worked this way).

items.title: Scrapbook text box: one border colour
items.detail: The text box uses the same border on hover and when clicked into, so there is no colour jump.

items.title: Screenshot button
items.detail: A new Screenshot command (add it from Customize > Toolbar, under View) captures the script page you're looking at and saves it as a PNG.

items.title: New themes save when you click the Customize Save button
items.detail: Building a theme and clicking the dialog’s Save now adds it to the list (the View menu and the Themes tab) — you no longer have to find the separate "Save Theme" button first.

items.title: Theme editor: the color picker no longer opens off-screen
items.detail: The swatch + hex column is pulled in from the right edge and the picker popup opens into that space on the right, so it stays on screen.

items.title: Smaller zoom − / + buttons
items.detail: The step buttons on the zoom control are smaller.

items.title: Add / Remove Scene Numbers is one toggle
items.detail: The ribbon/customize command is now a single "Scene Numbers" toggle (the menu already was), matching how it works everywhere.

items.title: Toggling the sizing lock no longer nudges the layout
items.detail: The lock icon now sits in a fixed square, so switching between the open and closed padlocks keeps the button the same size instead of pushing the panels and editor up and down.

items.title: Scrapbook ribbon + window tidy-up
items.detail: The "Scrapbook:" label is left-aligned; Return to Editor is a single blue button (icon beside two lines of text) in the ribbon — the duplicate one on the canvas is gone; and in the Scrapbook window the declutter (eye) toggle sits left with the create buttons on the right.

items.title: The sizing-lock button shows its state
items.detail: As a big ribbon button it now reads "Unlocked" with an open padlock when sizing is unlocked, and "Locked" with a closed padlock when locked (its palette name stays "Lock All").

items.title: Moving a ribbon section across the split no longer drags another section over
items.detail: When you move a section from the left-aligned run to the right (or vice versa), only that section changes sides now — the section that used to get pushed across to fill its place stays put.

items.title: Big ribbon buttons share one icon height
items.detail: Two-row / big buttons pin their icon to a fixed height, so every icon+label button measures the same top-to-bottom instead of varying with the icon.

items.title: "Lock Sizing" renamed to "Lock All"
items.detail: The toolbar button that freezes every chrome resize is now labelled Lock All.

items.title: Scrapbook: Return to Editor is a two-row ribbon button
items.detail: While the Scrapbook is open, "Return to Editor" now sits in the Scrapbook ribbon section as a two-row big button (icon + label) beside Insert Picture and Insert Table.

items.title: Asset Manager & Spell Check gone from the side panels for good
items.detail: They are no longer offered as side-panel tools AND no longer render in a dock even if a saved layout had them there — so an old file can no longer leave them stuck in the sidebar.

items.title: Trimmed the ribbon customize palette
items.detail: Spell Check, Writing Suggestions, Take Auto Save, Compare with Auto Save and AI Writer are no longer offered as ribbon buttons.

items.title: Section titles centred; titled rows sit a little lower
items.detail: Ribbon section titles are centred again, and when a section has a title its first row of items drops a few px to give the title room.

items.title: Undo works while clicked into the toolbar during edit mode
items.detail: Cmd/Ctrl+Z now undoes ribbon edits even when the script editor still holds focus — previously it only worked when focus was in the Customize window.

items.title: Fixed dragging the window by the title bar
items.detail: The Quick Access strip that fills most of the title bar row was not a drag surface (Tauri v2 only drags the exact element under the pointer), so most of the bar could not move the window. The whole row is draggable again — the QAT buttons still click as normal.

items.title: Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes ribbon edits while customizing the toolbar
items.detail: While the toolbar is being edited, undo now reverts your last ribbon change (add/remove/move a section or item, resize a spacer, the align split, …) instead of undoing the script. Typing in a section-title field still gets normal text undo.

items.title: Align Split is a bubble centred in the gap
items.detail: While editing the ribbon, the alignment split now reads as a block/bubble the size of a section, sitting halfway between the left-aligned run and the right-aligned run instead of as a small button by the right group.

items.title: Tighter rows and full-height dividers in the ribbon
items.detail: The gap between a two-row section's rows is smaller, and full-height section dividers now run all the way to the top and bottom of the ribbon.

items.title: Help menu: one "Feedback" item replaces Report a Bug / Feature Request
items.detail: The separate Report a Bug and Feature Request items are gone; a single Feedback item opens the feedback form the same in-app way.

items.title: Ribbon spacers can shrink to 5px
items.detail: The minimum spacer width is now 5px (was 8), and the edit-mode bar can be dragged down that far — the resize grip overhangs the edge so it stays grabbable.

items.title: Ribbon spacer now renders as a real bar
items.detail: The edit-mode spacer was collapsing to a flat dashed line because it had no height; it now has an explicit height and a solid accent fill, so it shows as a proper bar with the drag-to-resize grip on its right edge.

items.title: Ribbon spacers are drag-resizeable
items.detail: While editing the toolbar, a spacer now has a grip on its right edge — drag it to set the spacer's width (8–400px). The width is saved with the spacer, and it stays invisible on the live bar.

items.title: Spacers are easier to see and grab while editing
items.detail: The edit-mode spacer bubble is now brighter (an accent-tinted fill and border instead of a dim gray) and has a minimum width, so even a narrow spacer is easy to spot and grab. It is still invisible on the live bar.

items.title: Double-clicking a palette item adds it to the section you just made
items.detail: When editing the ribbon, double-clicking an item now drops it into the most recently created or edited section, instead of always the last (right-aligned) section.

items.title: Section titles: white, left-aligned, and the bar grows to fit them
items.detail: A section title is now white and left-aligned with more space below it, and adding one makes the whole ribbon taller (rather than overflowing) — the full-height section dividers stretch to match and sections stay vertically centered.

items.title: Spacers are visible while editing the ribbon
items.detail: A spacer now shows as a dimmed section-style bubble while the toolbar is being edited, so you can find and grab it; it stays completely invisible on the live bar.

items.title: Editor View button sized to the whole two-row span
items.detail: The Editor View button now measures — from the top of its dropdown box to the bottom of the "Editor View" text — exactly the distance from a row-1 item's text top to a row-2 item's text bottom, rather than just the dropdown alone.

items.title: Removing a ribbon section deletes it cleanly instead of merging
items.detail: Closing a section now removes just that section (and its own divider) and leaves the neighbours as separate sections — no more "extra long" merged section, and the alignment split / the other side stay put.

items.title: "Go to Last Edited" (renamed) now centres the spot on screen
items.detail: The old "Last Edit Location" command is renamed to "Go to Last Edited" and, instead of nudging the line barely into view, it scrolls so the last-edited line sits in the middle of the editor.

items.title: Editor View button: the dropdown spans both ribbon rows
items.detail: The big Editor View dropdown is now as tall as a top-row item through a bottom-row item, matching the two-row button.

items.title: Zoom control: dropped the magnifying-glass icon on the small version
items.detail: The inline zoom now shows just the − % + stepper (the big version already had no icon).

items.title: Asset Manager and Spell Check are no longer side-panel options
items.detail: They no longer appear in Customize > Side Panels; they open from the Tools menu / as their own windows instead.

items.title: Closing a ribbon section no longer drags the right-aligned run leftward
items.detail: Removing a section on the left of the alignment split used to merge it into the first right-aligned section and collapse the split, so the right-aligned sections jumped over to the left. A section now closes into a neighbour on its OWN side of the split (or clears itself if it is the only one there), leaving the other side untouched.

items.title: Scrapbook ribbon section: Insert Picture replaces New Page / New Section
items.detail: The Scrapbook section on the toolbar dropped its New Section and New Page buttons (both still live in the Scrapbook panel header) and gained an Insert Picture button beside Insert Table.

items.title: Removed the "Pages" title above the Scrapbook list
items.detail: The Scrapbook panel header no longer prints "Pages" above the sections and pages; the create buttons keep to the right.

items.title: Status bar hides script info while the Scrapbook is open
items.detail: With the Scrapbook active, the bottom bar no longer shows the current element, page count, act, runtime, revision or goal — those describe the script, not the notebook. The file name, save status and account chip stay.

items.title: Removed the empty row between every tool header and its contents
items.detail: Docked tool windows reserved a 26px top strip for a pop-out button that has actually lived in the header row since v1.80 — so it was just dead space. Dropped it everywhere, so every tool’s content sits flush under its header (the Scenes tool already had this).

items.title: Title Page: the two size selects are now the same width
items.detail: Title Size and Title Line 2 Size share a fixed width so they line up instead of sizing to their labels.

items.title: Title Page: the Delete Title Page button has a red background
items.detail: The destructive Delete Title Page button now carries a red tint so it reads apart from Preview/Cancel/Apply.

items.title: Scene list no longer shifts when its scrollbar disappears
items.detail: Stretching the Scenes window tall enough that the list fits made the scrollbar vanish and nudged every row and icon a few pixels right. The scrollbar gutter is now always reserved, so the list stays put whether or not it can scroll.

items.title: Title Page: point-size sits on the same row as its title
items.detail: Title Size now rides at the right of the Title row, and Title Line 2 Size shares the Title Line 2 row, instead of dropping onto their own lines below.

items.title: Fixed resizing the Scenes tool jumping to a huge empty height
items.detail: Dragging the bottom of the Scenes window to resize it grabbed the search footer instead of the scene list, so the window ballooned with a big gap between the list and the search bar. The drag now resizes the list body, and the list stretches to fill the taller window instead of leaving dead space.

items.title: Scenes tool header: count on the left, reading "Scenes: N"
items.detail: The scene count moved from the right side of the Scenes window header to the left edge and now reads "Scenes: N" (e.g. "Scenes: 8"). The filter funnel stays right-aligned where it was.

items.title: Scenes list sits flush under its header
items.detail: Removed the dead strip between the Scenes window header and the first scene — the list now starts right below the count/filter row.

items.title: Split the giant screenplay stylesheet into area files
items.detail: screenplay.css was one ~18,000-line stylesheet; it is now a barrel index that imports 25 area files (toolbar, scene navigator, tools/dock, outline bar, print, settings, …) under styles/screenplay/. Pure housekeeping — the compiled CSS is byte-for-byte identical, so nothing looks or behaves differently; editing a single area is just faster now.

items.title: Scenes tool: count & filter up top, search at the bottom
items.detail: The Scenes tool now matches the other tool windows — the scene count and the filter live in the window header, and the search is a footer bar. The old in-panel title/filter strip and floating search bar are gone.

items.title: Opening a script no longer marks it changed
items.detail: The scene-heading auto-uppercase now only fires on your edits, not when a script loads. Opening an older script with lowercase headings leaves it clean (nothing to save) — the headings still snap to caps the moment you touch them.

items.title: Outline Bar is fixed to its default rows
items.detail: The Customize > Outline Bar tab is gone — the bar always shows the four rows (Page Ruler, Sections, Beats, Scenes). You can still show/hide the bar from the View menu and drag its bottom edge to scale the rows.

items.title: No more duplicate ribbon items
items.detail: The Customize “add to the ribbon” list showed the same feature more than once — Title Page appeared three times (it exists as a button, a command and a tool). The list now shows each item exactly once.

items.title: Lock All / Reset All move to the footer
items.detail: In the Customize window, Lock All and Reset All now sit on the bottom row with Cancel and Save — the two of them on the left, Cancel/Save on the right.

items.title: Toolbar search shares the Show/Hide row
items.detail: The item search in Customize > Toolbar is now a fixed 300px, pinned to the right end of the Show/Hide row instead of a full-width bar on its own line.

items.title: Drag to reorder Outline Bar rows
items.detail: Customize > Outline Bar rows now reorder by dragging the row itself — the ↑/↓ arrows are gone. Drag a row’s bottom edge still sets its height.

items.title: “Move to Snippets” in the context menu
items.detail: The right-click “Copy to Snippets” is now “Move to Snippets” — it cuts the selection into a snippet card (one undo puts it back).

items.title: Spacers are visible while editing the toolbar
items.detail: A spacer is an invisible gap on the live bar, which made it a pain to find in the editor. While editing the toolbar, spacers now show a faint dashed outline and a “spacer” label so you can spot and grab them.

items.title: Taller Editor View dropdown
items.detail: The big Editor View dropdown is now 50% taller.

items.title: No caret on the big Zoom button
items.detail: The ▾ next to the zoom percentage is gone from the big Zoom button — Reset, Fit Page and Scale to Max Width all live in the View ▸ Zoom menu.

items.title: A title field over every ribbon section
items.detail: While editing the toolbar, each section now shows a “title” field on top — just type to name it, no adding a title from + Add and no dragging one around. Leave a field blank and nothing shows on the saved bar.

items.title: Save & Cancel on the Customize window
items.detail: The Customize window now has Save and Cancel buttons. Cancel puts every customization — ribbon layout, Quick Access, menu bar, panels, sizes, the Outline Bar — back to how it looked when you opened the window. Closing with the X while you have unsaved changes asks whether to Save, not save (“Don’t Save”), or keep editing.

items.title: Edit the zoom % right in the bar
items.detail: Clicking the zoom percentage now turns it into an input in place — no popup that just repeated the same stepper. A small ▾ still holds Reset / Fit Page / Scale to Max Width.

items.title: Fit button no longer stays lit blue
items.detail: One-shot ribbon commands (like Fit) now drop their focus ring after running, so they stop holding a blue highlight the way a toggle would.

items.title: Editor View label sits under its dropdown
items.detail: On the big Editor View button the “Editor View” label (no colon) now sits beneath the dropdown, matching the other big buttons.

items.title: Cleaner big Zoom button
items.detail: The large Zoom control drops its magnifier glyph — the percentage and the “Zoom” label already say what it is.

items.title: Editor View dropdown back to its old size
items.detail: Reverted the enlarged single-row Editor View control.

items.title: “Reset Customizations” confirmation
items.detail: Reset All now asks you to type “Reset Customizations” instead of “Reset Everything”.

items.title: Scene headings are really uppercase
items.detail: Scene heading text is now stored in caps, not just shown that way — so the Location tool, the scene list, search and Fountain/PDF export all see real uppercase. Older lowercase headings fix themselves the moment you touch them, and the Location tool shows every name in caps regardless.

items.title: Smarter element autofill
items.detail: The autofill list now appears the moment you’re in an empty Character, Scene Heading or Transition — no need to type a letter first. Scene headings suggest INT. / EXT. (with a space added after), then every location from the Location tool. Transitions suggest CUT TO:, DISSOLVE TO:, FADE IN:, FADE OUT:, FADE TO:, INTERCUT:, CUT TO BLACK:.

items.title: Parentheticals auto-wrap
items.detail: Adding a parenthetical drops in “()” with your cursor already between them.

items.title: Preview from the Title Page window
items.detail: A Preview button applies the title page and jumps you to Preview view, where it actually shows.

items.title: A little room under the ribbon
items.detail: 2px of padding between the ribbon buttons and the bar’s bottom edge.

items.title: No more blank page after a title page
items.detail: In Page view, adding a title page left the first script element stranded alone on an otherwise-blank page 1 while everything else jumped to page 2. The title page still shows only in Preview — but the editing views now flow straight from the top, no phantom page.

items.title: Titles belong to a section now
items.detail: Adding a Title from + Add drops it INTO the nearest section, on top of that section’s rows — no separate floating row. Edit the text inline, × to remove.

items.title: Toggle the side panels from the ribbon
items.detail: Two new ribbon items — Toggle Left Panel and Toggle Right Panel — under View in the palette.

items.title: Visual Outline Bar editor
items.detail: Customize > Outline Bar is now a visual stack: each row is a block sized to its real height — drag its bottom edge to resize. The four built-in rows (Page Ruler, Sections, Beats, Scenes) keep their names; only rows you add can be renamed. “Script Scenes” is now just “Scenes”.

items.title: Hover an item to see its name
items.detail: While editing the toolbar, hovering an item shows its name instead of a generic tip.

items.title: Cleaner Customize > Toolbar palette
items.detail: The structural utilities left the palette — they’re added from the bar’s own + Add. The Customize window opens 10px below the ribbon.

items.title: Bigger Editor View button
items.detail: The large single-row Editor View dropdown gets a roomier window; its field and caption stand as tall as any other one-row button.

items.title: Scrapbook polish
items.detail: The rule under a page title runs half-width; the title lines up with Return to Editor; less gap between the panel header and the first folder; and the ribbon’s SCRAPBOOK tag is centred over its buttons with more room on the left.

items.title: Title Page buttons off the edge
items.detail: Delete / Cancel / Apply no longer sit flush against the window’s bottom edge.

items.title: Titles are a placeable ribbon utility now
items.detail: Instead of belonging to one two-row section, a Title is an item you add from + Add. Titles live in a row ABOVE the sections; add as many as you like and drop spacers between them to slide each title over the section it labels. Drag to reorder, type to rename, × to remove.

items.title: Each ribbon utility shows what it looks like
items.detail: The + Add menu draws a little picture of every utility — a one- or two-row box, a divider line, a dashed spacer, the split, an “Aa” title — so you can pick by shape, not just by name.

items.title: “+ Add” leads with the utilities
items.detail: The on-bar + Add menu now lists the structural pieces up front — 1 Row Section, 2 Row Section, Divider, Spacer, Alignment Split — with everything else tucked behind an “Add Item ›” submenu (searchable, by category). Less to wade through when all you want is a divider.

items.title: Dividers and spacers in the Quick Access Toolbar
items.detail: Customize > Quick Access now has Add Divider and Add Spacer — drop a thin line or a blank gap between the titlebar buttons and drag it where you want, just like the ribbon.

items.title: Name your Outline Bar rows
items.detail: Each row in Customize > Outline Bar has an editable name — type over “Beats” to call it whatever you like. Blank falls back to the default. The name shows on the bar.

items.title: Tab help tucked into an info button
items.detail: Every Customize tab’s instructions moved out of the way into a single ?-in-a-circle in the tab’s upper-right corner. Click it when you want the guidance; otherwise the tab stays clean.

items.title: Add anything to the ribbon from the bar itself
items.detail: While editing the toolbar, a faint “+ Add” block appears at the end of the left-aligned run and — if you have an align split — at the start of the right-aligned run. Click it for a searchable menu that builds a 1-row section, a 2-row section, a divider, a spacer, an alignment split, or any item (button, dropdown, tool) — all from the same list the Customize palette uses.

items.title: Name your two-row sections
items.detail: A two-row section can carry a title/descriptor underneath (like Word’s ribbon-group labels). Type it in the field under the section while editing; it shows on the live bar. One-row sections skip it — their buttons already read as words.

items.title: Steadier item placement
items.detail: The drop indicator no longer flutters back and forth when you hover a spot — placement is read from the items’ own positions, so it stays put instead of fighting the indicator it just drew.

items.title: Section-close no longer collides with an item’s ×
items.detail: The button that closes a section moved to the section’s top-left corner, clear of the last item’s remove ×.

items.title: Editor View button stops repeating its name
items.detail: The big “Editor View” dropdown showed its label twice — it already captions itself, so the duplicate underneath is gone.

items.title: The toolbar spotlights itself while editing
items.detail: Open Customize > Toolbar and the rest of the app dims and locks out — only the ribbon (now ringed in the accent color) and the Customize window stay bright and usable, so it's obvious what you can touch.

items.title: Reset All asks you to type it
items.detail: Resetting every customization now requires typing “Reset Everything” — the button stays dead until it matches. No more one-click wipe of your whole layout.

items.title: Customize the toolbar ON the toolbar
items.detail: No more separate mini-preview to second-guess. Open Customize > Toolbar and the REAL ribbon becomes the editor: drag items and utilities from the window straight onto the bar, drag a section by its body to move it, hover an item or section for its ×, drag an item off the bar to remove it. Close the window and the layout locks. What you edit is the bar itself, so it always matches.

items.title: Lock All / Reset All, side by side
items.detail: The two global Customize buttons are shorter and sit in one row.

items.title: Quick Access icons truly the same height
items.detail: Sized from each glyph's MEASURED drawn extent instead of its font box — icon glyphs fill anywhere from 75% to 100% of their boxes, which is why Open and Save read smaller. Every icon now draws at the same visual height.

items.title: Drag a dropdown's edge to set its width
items.detail: In the visual editor, grab the right edge of the font, size, element or Editor View field and drag. The width applies to the REAL ribbon instantly — one setting drives both — and Reset All Customizations clears it.

items.title: Lock/Reset cover ALL customizations
items.detail: "Lock All Sizing" is now "Lock All Customizations" — while locked, every Customize tab is veiled, not just resize handles. "Reset All Sizes" is "Reset All Customizations" — sizes, toolbar layout, dropdown widths, Quick Access, menu bar order, side panels and the Outline Bar all return to factory (after a confirm). Both read as real buttons now.

items.title: Scrapbook toolbar section grows
items.detail: New Section and New Page ride beside Insert Table — the same actions as the panel header, one tap from the ribbon.

items.title: Scrapbook title font restored
items.detail: Back to the app's own title style (the OneNote-inspired light face read as foreign); the rule under it is brighter, and the "empty — drop pages here" hint is gone from the tree.

items.title: Toolbar tab helper text → ? icon
items.detail: The paragraph under the strip is gone; a ? button by the utilities holds the condensed version.

items.title: Editor strip: native stepper chevrons + tighter rows
items.detail: Dropdown chips draw the macOS up/down stepper like real selects, and section internals (row gaps, the split line) match the live bar's spacing.

items.title: Editor strip matches the bar, to the pixel
items.detail: Chips are the live buttons' exact size (26×24, 12px glyphs, 28px rows, 24px dropdown fields) and sit flat like the real bar — the grab highlight only appears on hover. Big-button icons match the live 29px too.

items.title: Scrapbook tools are back on the ribbon — permanently
items.detail: While the Scrapbook is open, a SCRAPBOOK section (tag + its tools) is injected as the last left-aligned section, whatever your saved layout says. It used to depend on a token surviving in the layout — close that section in Customize and the tools silently vanished.

items.title: Scrapbook page title, OneNote style
items.detail: A large light title over a rule, with the full date ("Friday, July 17, 2026") and the creation time beneath — the time follows your 12/24-hour setting.

items.title: Menus get a minimum width
items.detail: macOS sizes a native menu to its widest item, so menus full of short names (Tools) came out skinny. Every menu now pads out to a comfortable minimum width.

items.title: Editor dropdowns match the bar's lengths
items.detail: Each dropdown chip in the visual editor now carries its live counterpart's width — the font field is as long as the real font field, and so on.

items.title: Ribbon edge padding back to 12px
items.detail: The v3.28 doubling is walked back — the real culprit (the Customize button sizing only to its icon) was fixed in v3.29.

items.title: Tool-specific items out of the palette
items.detail: Insert Table (Scrapbook) is no longer offered in Customize > Toolbar — it only ever worked inside the Scrapbook. Layouts that already have it keep it.

items.title: Editor rows match the real ribbon
items.detail: In a two-row section the dropdown row rendered about half the height of the button row. Rows are a fixed, equal height now — like the live bar — and dropdown fields stand as tall as every other chip.

items.title: Leaner ribbon palette
items.detail: The File category is gone from Customize > Toolbar — File actions belong to the Quick Access Toolbar (Customize > Quick Access). Dual Dialogue left too; it's an element, inserted from the Insert menu. Anything already pinned keeps working.

items.title: The ribbon editor is WYSIWYG
items.detail: The strip in Customize > Toolbar now mirrors the real bar: items in a single-row section render big (large icon, name underneath), and the dropdown fields — font, size, element, Editor View, zoom — look like the dropdowns they are, resting text and all.

items.title: Section drops track the cursor
items.detail: Dragging a section or block, the insertion line leaped to the strip's end whenever the pointer crossed the gap BETWEEN sections — placing one mid-strip meant aiming way left. The boundary now comes from geometry (nearest section midpoints), so the line stays with the cursor.

items.title: Close-section × on the section itself
items.detail: It rides the section bubble's top-right corner now (hover to see it) instead of hanging off the divider line. The divider is just a divider.

items.title: Customize opens below the ribbon
items.detail: The window's default position clears the whole toolbar so you can see your edits land live. Still draggable anywhere.

items.title: Divider no longer overlaps Customize at custom scale
items.detail: With a dragged toolbar height, the width clamp meant for small buttons squeezed the tall Customize button under its own label, which painted over the divider beside it. Big and tall buttons now size to their content in every mode.

items.title: Apply stays inside the color picker
items.detail: The hex field refused to shrink (a text input's intrinsic width) and shoved the Apply button out of the popup's edge.

items.title: More air at the ribbon's right edge
items.detail: The right-aligned tail (Customize) gets 24px of padding from the window edge — v3.10's 12px still read as touching.

items.title: No divider at the ribbon's edges
items.detail: A section left empty (say, by dropping the align split at the end) still painted its boundary line — a stray divider left of the first item or right of the last. The live bar now skips empty sections and their dividers entirely; they remain visible in the Customize editor so you can fill them.

items.title: Align Split drops between sections
items.detail: It behaves like the section blocks now — drag it to a boundary (the same drop line sections use) instead of into a section's item row.

items.title: Keyboard Shortcuts is no longer a ribbon option
items.detail: Removed from the Customize palette (its Help category went with it, now empty). A copy already pinned to your toolbar keeps working.

items.title: New Script window centers on the screen
items.detail: It sat high — dialogs anchor toward the top by default. The hero card now centers vertically, and still scrolls if it ever outgrows the window.

items.title: Panel collapse chevrons removed
items.detail: The slim collapse row atop each side panel is gone. Hide panels from View > Toolbars; a collapsed panel still re-opens from the strip on its edge.

items.title: The A always wears the chosen text color
items.detail: The Text Color icon defaulted to red. It now matches whatever color is picked — black when black — everywhere, all the time.

items.title: One item per on/off feature
items.detail: Everything with a show/hide or on/off dichotomy is a single menu item with a checkmark now — Scene Numbers, Show Rulers, the Working Notes toggles, Auto Spell Check, the Editor views, themes and workspaces. No more Add/Remove or Show/Hide pairs anywhere.

items.title: Bookmarks removed
items.detail: Markers already cover the job. The bookmark list, its menu and the editor gutter marks are gone; Last Edit Location survives and moved to the Edit menu (still pinnable to the ribbon and reachable from Customize).

items.title: Production Tags moved to Insert
items.detail: Tagging is something you do to the script, so it sits with markers and notes now. The Customize palette mirrors the move. Customize… also moved to the top of the View menu.

items.title: Every window wears the same header and footer
items.detail: The Save As treatment is the app-wide standard: dialog headers and footers share the toolbar's chrome surface with no divider lines, and the resize-grip strip below the footer is painted to match.

items.title: Scrapbook header un-stretched
items.detail: A leftover width rule from before the created-date line existed was being read as a HEIGHT, ballooning the title box to 320px and shoving the title, the created date and Return to Editor way off position. The header is back to one tidy row — name on top, "Created …" right under it.

items.title: Outline: Freeform cards no longer spawn stacked — linking works
items.detail: Every beat was created at the canvas origin, so Freeform piled them all onto one spot and the Connect drag could never reach a second card. Beats you haven't placed now cascade into a grid; drag one anywhere and it keeps that spot.

items.title: Ribbon dropdowns scale with the bar
items.detail: Font, size, element and Editor View fields track the exact button height in every toolbar size, including edge-drag scaling — they were stuck at fixed heights. The side-panel toggle buttons are retired (the collapse chevrons and View > Toolbars cover them), and the QAT's Save icons get an optical size correction so nothing reads bigger than its neighbors.

items.title: Auto Save locations explained
items.detail: Settings > Save now says what each local row actually is: the version history lives inside the app (browse it from Project > Script History), while the Local folder row writes real timestamped .odraft files to a folder you choose.

items.title: Donate button 20% bigger
items.detail: In About ScriptCraft.

items.title: Dev Picker removed
items.detail: The development-only inspector tool is gone — code, styles, panel registration and its Help menu entry.

items.title: Leaner menus
items.detail: Production merged into Project (Title Page, Set Draft Number, Scene Numbers, Revision Mode, Production Tags live there now); Add/Remove Scene Numbers is one checkable toggle; Subscript/Superscript and File > Preview are gone; Lock/Reset All Sizing moved into the Customize window; Grammar & Spelling Settings opens from Settings; Changelog lives in About as "What's New". Eight menus, down from nine.

items.title: Customize palette mirrors the new menus
items.detail: The Production category folded into Project; the empty Format category is gone.

items.title: Sections drag by their body
items.detail: Grab a section bubble anywhere that isn't an item and move it — the grip handle is gone, and sections read as blocks. New Row is retired; the Two Rows block covers it.

items.title: Color for big buttons only
items.detail: Small one-row-tall ribbon buttons are back to monotone; large single-row buttons keep their colors.

items.title: Color comes to the ribbon
items.detail: Ribbon icons wear tasteful single colors — amber undo/redo, blue clipboard and file actions, yellow notes, green to-dos, teal find, the pink Customize wrench. Menus, panels and everything else stay monotone.

items.title: Build the ribbon from section blocks
items.detail: The customizer's utilities now lead with two blocks — Single Row and Two Rows. Drop one anywhere on the strip and an empty section of that shape appears there (double-click adds one at the end); dividers between adjacent sections draw themselves. New Row stays for splitting an existing section at a chosen spot.

items.title: Customize the Quick Access Toolbar
items.detail: A new Quick Access tab in Customize — the same Shown/Hidden columns as the other tabs. Twelve options, mostly File actions: Save, Save As, Open, New, Undo, Redo, Print, Preview, Export PDF, Spell Check, Find & Replace, Add Bookmark. Order is drag-to-arrange and persists.

items.title: Titlebar script name truly centered
items.detail: The document title centers on the window itself, so the number of Quick Access buttons can't push it off-center.

items.title: Customize matches the other big buttons
items.detail: In a one-row section, Customize is one button block with its label inside — same format and size as every other large button.

items.title: Text Color and Highlight Color work again
items.detail: Their pickers opened INSIDE the ribbon, which clips its overflow — so they were invisible and the buttons looked dead. They now open in front of everything, anchored under the button.

items.title: The A wears the picked color
items.detail: The Text Color icon tints to whatever color is selected (red until you pick one).

items.title: Room between big buttons
items.detail: Single-row ribbon sections space their buttons further apart.

items.title: Right-aligned sections fill right-to-left
items.detail: Double-click-adding into a section right of the align split inserts at the front, so the anchor button (Customize) keeps its place at the edge.

items.title: One control row in the toolbar customizer
items.detail: Show/Hide, Reset to Default Size and the structural utilities (+ Section, New Row, Divider, Spacer, Align Split) share a single row above the editor.

items.title: Leaner customize palette
items.detail: Thirteen weak toolbar candidates are no longer offered: Subscript, Superscript, Reset Sizing, Select All, the three imports, Settings, Script Format Preferences, Grammar & Spelling Settings, and the Help one-shots (About, Feature Request, Report a Bug, Changelog, Knowledge Base). Anything already pinned in your layout keeps working — only the option to add them is gone.

items.title: Donate button in the About footer
items.detail: Buy Me a Coffee sits bottom-left of the About window, inline with Close — back in the yellow pill with the white cup.

items.title: Reorder whole ribbon sections
items.detail: Each section in the customizer has a grip at its left edge — drag it to move the entire section, with an insertion line showing where it will land. Items, rows and the align split all travel with it.

items.title: Bookmarks live under Project
items.detail: The Bookmarks menu moved from the top level into Project > Bookmarks — same contents: add, remove, Last Edit Location, and the jump list.

items.title: View > Toolbars
items.detail: The Left Panel, Right Panel and Outline Bar toggles group under one Toolbars submenu, with checkmarks in the check column.

items.title: New Script: Format field height
items.detail: The Format dropdown now stands as tall as the other fields — WebKit's native select was ignoring the padding the text boxes use.

items.title: Bigger single-row ribbon buttons
items.detail: Big-button icons are 50% larger (19px → 29px) — Customize and every other item in a one-row section. That icon-plus-label height is the single-row standard.

items.title: One About, in the right place
items.detail: ScriptCraft > About ScriptCraft now opens the full About window (version, credits, compatibility) instead of macOS's stock panel, and Help no longer duplicates it. With in-window menus, Help keeps the item — there's no app menu there to hold it.

items.title: Donate button moved into About
items.detail: The Buy Me a Coffee button leaves the titlebar and lives in the About ScriptCraft window.

items.title: FreeScript → ScriptCraft, everywhere it was left
items.detail: The splash screen (it still said FreeScript and OPEN DRAFT), the Dev Picker's storage keys (with a one-time migration so drafts survive), and the docs. The repo itself renames on GitHub — old links redirect.

items.title: Donate button recolored
items.detail: The titlebar's Buy Me a Coffee button follows the updated design: cyan pill, yellow cup, black text.

items.title: Buy Me a Coffee button in the titlebar
items.detail: The donation button — yellow pill, cup and all — sits at the far right of the Quick Access Toolbar row and opens the donation page in your default browser. The Help menu link stays too.

items.title: Search the customizer palette
items.detail: A keyword filter above the available items — type "save" and every category narrows to Save, Save As, the auto-save commands, and so on. Clearing it restores the full list.

items.title: Section dividers survive toolbar scaling
items.detail: Dragging the toolbar edge to scale it collapsed the two-row section dividers to single-row height (a leftover rule from the pre-ribbon bar). They now span and scale with the ribbon.

items.title: Breathing room at the ribbon's right edge
items.detail: The right-aligned tail (Customize) sat flush against the window edge — the ribbon now keeps a 12px inset.

items.title: Quick Access Toolbar in the titlebar
items.detail: Word-style: the macOS titlebar is now part of the app — Save, Undo and Redo sit beside the traffic lights, with the document title centered where macOS used to draw it. The whole strip still drags and double-click-zooms the window.

items.title: Donation link is "Buy Me a Coffee"
items.detail: Renamed from the pizza wording, per the updated button.

items.title: Bookmarks
items.detail: A new Bookmarks menu (native and in-window). Add Bookmark drops a named jump point at the cursor — it keeps pointing at the same text as the script changes. Clicking a bookmark jumps there; Remove Bookmark clears one. Both actions are also pinnable to the ribbon.

items.title: Last Edit Location
items.detail: The Bookmarks menu's permanent first jump: return to wherever the script was last actually changed — not necessarily the end.

items.title: Buy Me a Coffee
items.detail: A donation link at the end of the Help menu, opening in your default browser.

items.title: Two more checkmarks moved to the check column
items.detail: Lock Scene Numbers and Revision Mode (Production menu) now use the v3.05 check column instead of a ✓ label prefix.

items.title: Collapse buttons atop the side panels
items.detail: Obsidian-style: each side panel has a double-chevron button at its top that collapses it. A slim strip stays at that edge to expand it back — the toolbar toggles and View menu still work too.

items.title: Outline Bar buttons reworked
items.detail: The side column now reads add → open Outline window → choose outline → send to script → fit. Fit is an icon like its neighbours, and the buttons keep their size when the bar is resized (the rows still scale).

items.title: Outline window opens popped out
items.detail: The bar's open-Outline-window button opens it as a floating window instead of docking it into the side panel.

items.title: Menu checkmarks get their own column
items.detail: Checkable menu items (highlight color, Auto Spell Check, Auto Writing Suggestions, Show Rulers) no longer prefix a ✓ to their label — the mark lives in a dedicated left column, macOS style, so labels stay aligned whether an item is checked or not. The native menu bar renders them as real check items.

items.title: Zoom in/out from the toolbar
items.detail: The zoom control gains − and + buttons either side of the dropdown trigger, so stepping the zoom no longer requires opening the menu. The current-zoom readout is a size smaller to keep the group compact.

items.title: Window before Help
items.detail: The native macOS menu bar now follows the platform convention: the Window menu sits before Help instead of trailing the whole bar. Retitling a window no longer shuffles it back to the end either.

items.title: Ribbon drag works everywhere
items.detail: The customize editor moved off the browser's native drag-and-drop (unreliable in the Mac app) to direct pointer tracking — chips in single-row sections, and everything else, now drag first time, with a small ghost riding the cursor.

items.title: Customize is a ribbon item
items.detail: The fixed Customize button is gone from the toolbar chrome. It's now a regular ribbon item — movable, removable, and re-addable from the palette. Saved layouts get it appended automatically so it doesn't vanish.

items.title: The last section can be closed
items.detail: Every section now carries its own closing divider with an ✕ — including the last one, which merges leftward.

items.title: Align Split utility
items.detail: A new utility splits the ribbon in two: sections before it hug the left edge, sections after it hug the right. The default layout uses it to keep Customize on the far right.

items.title: A new default ribbon — Derek's layout
items.detail: Fresh installs and Reset to Default now match the curated bar: Copy/Paste over Undo/Redo, font name and size over the styling and alignment row, the Element picker over the insert buttons, and big Find & Go-to buttons. Everything else waits in the Customize palette.

items.title: Text Color is a red A
items.detail: The toolbar button's underline bar carries whatever color is currently picked.

items.title: Double-click to add ribbon items
items.detail: Double-clicking a palette item (or the Divider/Spacer utilities) drops it straight into the most recently added or modified section — no drag needed.

items.title: Ribbon editor: no more squashed chips in narrow windows
items.detail: The visual editor never shrinks its sections now — when the window is too small, the strip scrolls horizontally instead of stacking icons on top of each other.

items.title: Ribbon editor: dragging is stable
items.detail: Two causes of the flicker-and-jump: the drop indicator used to take up real space, shifting the chips under your cursor so the target flip-flopped — it overlays the gap now. And after a successful drag, a leftover internal handler could fire a phantom second drag on the next mouse move, teleporting the item back — drags now hand off cleanly.

items.title: Fixed: some ribbon items refused to drag in Customize
items.detail: On the Mac, chips for items already on the bar could silently refuse to start dragging (removing and re-adding them "cured" it). The editor no longer depends on the system drag starting at all: if you press and move a chip and the native drag never kicks in, the editor runs the drag itself — same drop indicator, same result. Chips are also explicitly marked draggable for WebKit.

items.title: The whole menu is ribbon-pinnable now
items.detail: The v2.97 palette covered the common commands; this finishes the audit. New in Customize: Insert (Image, Marker), View (Scale to Fit Page, Scale to Max Width, Actual Size, Show/Hide Rulers), Format (Script Format Preferences), Help (About, Keyboard Shortcuts, Knowledge Base, Changelog, Feature Request, Report a Bug), plus the Word/PDF import variants, the ScriptCraft (.odraft) export and Grammar & Spelling Settings. Pickers with their own flows (Workspaces, Theme, Element) stay in the menus.

items.title: Fixed: "Scale to Max Width" could hang the app
items.detail: The v2.97 command-bus fallback made fitPage/fitWidth re-dispatch themselves in a loop. They are explicitly routed to the editor now.

items.title: One-row sections grow BIG buttons
items.detail: Word style: an item in a section with no row split renders as a large icon with its name underneath, the pair filling most of the section's height — exactly the Styles Pane / Dictate format from the reference. Two-row sections keep compact icons.

items.title: Every menu action is ribbon-pinnable
items.detail: New Script, Open, Import, Save, Save As, Print, Preview, all four exports, Settings, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All and Dual Dialogue join the Customize palette under File and Edit. One command bus runs them — the menu item, the keyboard shortcut and the ribbon button share a single closure.

items.title: Ribbon editor refinements
items.detail: The structural tools (New Row, Divider, Spacer) moved beside + Section. Spacers resize by dragging their right edge — the chip's width IS the spacer.
